reuse_policy: Two published actual case reports supplied reasoning mechanisms. The patient chats, numbers, chronology and answers are original synthetic material. No report text, images, actual-patient combinations, purchased question or Xi'an record is reproduced. No patient reconstruction is claimed.
language_note: Chinese was composed as a natural family conversation and checked against the English facts. The inherited machine_translation_unreviewed flag records absent professional language validation; it is not a claim that machine translation was used.
access_notes: The heart-failure report's full PMC text and the AHA official guideline landing page/slide set were opened. Recommendation tables on congestion/perfusion, continuation and decongestion were read as text. Browser PDF screenshots returned no image through the tool, so visual layout inspection is not claimed.
The nutrition report's PubMed abstract, publisher full PDF and indexed full PMC text were read. Some direct PMC opens returned a browser challenge; no challenge was bypassed.

AuSPEN's official 2025 resource page and complete consensus PDF, plus ASPEN's publisher full text, were read. ASPEN links an erratum that could not be opened; no dosing or corrected table transcription is imported. This limitation requires later source review.
NICE CG32 direct HTML/PDF opens returned 403. Indexed snippets suggest differing feeding conventions, but unseen NICE full text is not a verified source for these labels.
Two other nutrition reports (PMC5624659 and PMC7871053) were rejected as adaptation sources because their displayed licenses are CC BY-NC. Neither patient narrative nor numerical course is reused.
This is a bounded evidence check, not a complete current-guideline, correction/retraction, rights or privacy clearance. Recheck article status and exact versions before external clinical use.

records.inspiration_scope: The report illustrates how renal impairment and congestion can coexist and how an unsupported dehydration assumption may misdirect care. The new case instead tests a fictional monitored decongestion course and asks for balanced review. No original age, comorbidity combination, values, timeline, intervention or outcome is reused.

report.title: When Two Syndromes Collide: Managing Fanconi and Refeeding Syndrome in a Single Patient
report.authors: Gallegos Koyner FJ, Barrera N, Subedi P, Shrestha K, Cerrud-Rodriguez R
report.license_evidence: Publisher PDF page 1 and indexed PMC copyright section explicitly identify CC BY 4.0.
report.consent_status: consent obtained or waived; specific individual publication-consent status not resolved
report.status_check: PubMed identity and publisher article checked; complete correction/retraction and individual-consent verification remains pending. The 2023 CHEST abstract is the same report source group, not a second independent case.

records.inspiration_scope: The actual report highlights concurrent nutrition-related and other electrolyte mechanisms. The synthetic family uses a different, unspecified adult, new nutrition history and new values. The report's HIV, antiretroviral exposure, renal-wasting evidence, exact chronology, invasive procedures and fatal outcome are not reused; Fanconi syndrome or a drug cause is not an expected answer.

requirement_support.source_locator: Adult risk Table 3 and its normal-electrolyte footnote; corroborating AuSPEN 2025 section 3.2
requirement_support.basis: Nutritional history can confer risk with normal circulating electrolytes. This fictional history is not a diagnosed syndrome.
Team care, thiamine and serial biochemical/clinical surveillance are supported; exact grouping and partial-credit boundaries are authored.
Nutrition remains necessary and must be supervised. Societies differ on initial provision/advancement, so a fixed rate or prolonged low feeding is not keyed.

requirement_support.source_locator: Sections 3.3 and 3.7: symptomatic electrolyte change after nutrition
requirement_support.basis: The new intake, trajectory and symptoms warrant immediate clinical concern. Exact syndrome attribution/severity is not proven by the case.

requirement_support.source_locator: Sections 3.4, 3.6 and 3.7; report provides coexistence illustration only
requirement_support.basis: Supports monitored correction and assessing other contributors; no urine test, drug attribution or specific replacement dose is inferred.

requirement_support.source_locator: Section 3.5: stabilization before further advancement; compare ASPEN Table 6
requirement_support.basis: Both approaches support reassessment before further escalation with serious abnormalities. AuSPEN does not routinely require cessation; ASPEN allows reduction or temporary cessation for severe changes. Neither supports indefinite unplanned starvation.

records.critical_error_basis: Severity 2/3 and the exact affirmative boundaries are author proposals. Omissions alone do not establish the named escalation/starvation errors. A supervised temporary reduction or hold with reassessment is an acceptable clinical alternative, not an unsafe label.
records.privacy_and_leakage_check: Original synthetic values/history; no report patient demographics, rare identifiers or images. Public concept may be memorized. No Xi'an or purchased content. Not hidden Gold.

related_families.relationship: shared electrolyte/clinical-change reasoning but distinct nutrition mechanism and competing underfeeding risk

review_questions: Are the fictional intake, time course, symptoms and laboratory ranges clinically plausible and sufficiently informative?
Do acceptable supervised feeding alternatives fairly cover ASPEN/AuSPEN differences without rewarding indefinite underfeeding?
Does any requirement double-count escalation, monitoring or uncertainty?
Check exact source status/erratum, publication-consent disposition, severity, patient-facing detail and EN/ZH equivalence before promotion.
